name: Haverdal - Tylösand

officialSources.name: Hallandsleden: Haverdal - Tylösand
facts: Official name Haverdal - Tylösand.
Official distance 12.7 km.
Difficulty Grön, normalized here as easy.
No official estimated time shown.

Official description says the route starts at Haverdal's northern beach, crosses dunes and Haverdal nature reserve, passes Lynga sand dune, Vilshärad, Ringenäs, Frösakull, Tylebäck and Nyrebäcken, then ends at Tylösand beach.

officialSources.name: Länsstyrelsen Halland: Haverdal nature reserve
facts: Haverdal is one of Halland's oldest nature reserves and includes fly-sand fields, dunes, pine forest, trails and Stora Sandkullen/Lynga sand dune.
Facts on the page list Halmstad municipality, 632 hectares, protected since 1942 and 2013, Naturvårdsverket ownership, Länsstyrelsen management and Natura 2000 status.
Visitor rules include no tenting, dogs leashed, fires only at designated places, no horses on marked walking trails and no camper/caravan parking in the reserve 24.00-06.00.
Page warns about strong currents and sudden seabed changes in Haverdalsbukten and soft/quicksand-like sand near the shifting Skintan outlet.

officialSources.name: Halmstad municipality: Stränder och badplatser
facts: Halmstad municipality says beach toilets are open and rubbish is collected from June to September.
Haverdalsstrand, Vilshäradstrand, Ringenässtrand, Frösakullsstrand and Tylösands strand all have toilet/service context.
Tylösand, Frösakull, Ringenäs and Villshärad are summer-monitored by trained lifeguards; red flag means dangerous bathing.

officialSources.name: Halmstad municipality: Hundar och hästar på stranden
facts: Dogs are prohibited on municipal official bathing beaches between 1 May and 15 September.
Horses are prohibited on official bathing beaches between 1 May and 15 September and riding in sea-shore dunes is never allowed.
Dogs are welcome year-round on non-official beaches if under close control.

routeCharacter: Easy coastal stage with mixed dune/reserve paths, beach access, old coastal road, settlement-edge paths, coastal meadow and resort/beach endpoint.
Starts near Båtabacken/Haverdal and enters Haverdal nature reserve and dune terrain.
Passes Lynga/Stora Sandkullen, a 36 m dune viewpoint area with stairs and benches.
Continues past Vilshärad and along older coastal-road alignment before turning toward shallow Ringenäs beach.
Follows Frösakull coastal meadows and the Tylebäck/Nyrebäcken area.
Ends at Tylösand, a dense beach and resort-service endpoint.

Classified core facilities from Haverdal start toilets/parking, Haverdal/Lynga/Ringenäs/Frösakull/Tylösand toilets, beaches, parking, bus stops, Vilshärads Camping and endpoint services; kept off-route commercial services pending/suppressed and found no public water/fireplace/free shelter.

Confirmed Haverdalsvägen as primary start bus about 573-574 m from endpoint, Tylösand as primary end bus about 309-312 m from endpoint, strong Vilshärad/Ringenäs intermediate bus bailouts, endpoint parking candidates and no ferry/boat/rowboat dependency.

Found no active K6 closure/reroute; field evidence is mostly partial local routes around Haverdal reserve and Frösakull/Tylösand. Imported route-character and localized wet beach/soft sand/pinecone/stairs/strong-current caveats only.

Confirmed Haverdal reserve/Natura direct route span approx km 0.000-5.027, nearby Villshärad/Ringenäs/Tylön/Möllegård contexts, beach dog/horse/fire rules, Ringenäs military warning context, Tylösand future-works watch and no active official closure.
